title: Derived global sections of a derived direct image
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. For every open subscheme $U\subseteq Y$, with $f_U:f^{-1}U\to U$, there is a natural isomorphism $R\Gamma(U,R(f_U)_*(E|_{f^{-1}U}))\cong R\Gamma(f^{-1}U,E|_{f^{-1}U})$ of complexes of abelian groups; $R(f_U)_*$ is the derived direct image [def-pc-derived-direct-image] and $R\Gamma$ is the derived global-sections functor [def-sc-sheaf-cohomology-functor].

source.place: Tag 08D5 (perfect-lemma-quasi-coherence-direct-image), proof of part (2), displayed identity RΓ(U,Rf_*E)=RΓ(f^{-1}U,E)

proof.text: Fix an open subscheme U⊆Y and put V=f^{-1}U. By the definition of the underived direct image, Γ(U,(f_U)_*G)=Γ(V,G) naturally for every O_V-module sheaf G; this is the degree-zero section identity used in Tag 08D5.

source.place: Tag 08D5, proof of part (2), displayed identity Γ(U,f_*G)=Γ(f^{-1}U,G)

proof.text: Let P be the one-point ringed space (pt,Z) with structure sheaf the ring Z, so Mod(Z_P)=Ab. Let π_U:(U,O_U)→P and π_V:(V,O_V)→P be the morphisms of ringed spaces [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism] given by the constant map and the unique ring maps Z→O_U(U), Z→O_V(V). Uniqueness of ring maps out of Z gives π_V=π_U∘f_U as ringed-space morphisms (f_U is a morphism of schemes, hence of ringed spaces). By the direct image of [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image], (π_U)_*G=Γ(U,G) and (π_V)_*G=Γ(V,G); since R(π_U)_* is computed by applying (π_U)_* to any K-injective resolution, as is RΓ(U,-), we have RΓ(U,-)=R(π_U)_* and RΓ(V,-)=R(π_V)_* as functors to D(Ab). (Note P is not a scheme, and the structure morphism U→Spec Z would not do: its derived direct image lands in D(O_{Spec Z}), not in complexes of abelian groups.)

source.place: Tag 0D5T context: direct image to a one-point ringed space is global sections

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image-composition] to the composable morphisms of ringed spaces V→U→P (f_U then π_U). It gives R(π_U)_*∘R(f_U)_*≅R(π_U∘f_U)_*=R(π_V)_*. Evaluating at E|_V and using Step 2 yields RΓ(U,R(f_U)_*(E|_V))≅RΓ(V,E|_V), naturally in E; the identification is compatible with restriction to smaller opens U'⊆U by construction, giving naturality in U.
